## Stated values
> Be careful here. This is a Hub and, for instance, BayesianVAR depends on it.

Reading of that for the implementer: MacroEconometricTools is a **hub** package.
`BayesianVAR.jl` and `LocalProjections.jl` depend on it and consume its shared
result/spec types (`BayesianIRFResult`, `LocalProjectionIRFResult`,
`BayesianVAR`, `MinnesotaPrior`, `LocalProjection`, …) and its matrix-level
structural-core functions. **Any rename, unexport, or signature change must be
checked against spoke usage first** — a change that is "non-breaking" for a
direct user of the hub can still break a spoke that imports the name. Treat
every breaking chunk as potentially breaking downstream and audit
`BayesianVAR.jl` / `LocalProjections.jl` before implementing it.

- **Central abstraction**: `VARModel{T,S}` + `AbstractIdentification`.
- **Error model**: fail-fast — throw on bad input, no silent sentinels.

## Release strategy
- **Pre-breaking-release**: `yes` — cut a final non-breaking release before the
  first breaking change, then batch all breaking work into one terminal
  breaking release.
- **Inter-cluster releases**: `no` — batch into a single terminal breaking
  release.

## Decisions
<!-- Answers to `decide` chunks land here, with the chunk ID. -->
- CHUNK-005 (bootstrap_irf* family): leave exported as-is; document the
  relationship to the `inference=` path only. No restructuring. (Author
  decision at review time.)
- Export-surface restructuring: author chose **drop placeholders only** — do not
  move spoke/advanced names to `public`. Only the empty `NormalWishartPrior`
  placeholder is removed (CHUNK-004).
- CHUNK-003 (narrative dates API): author chose to store dates **on the hub
  `VARModel`** (in `metadata`, fetched via a new exported `dates(model)`
  accessor) rather than passing a `dates=` kwarg to `irf`. Dates are supplied
  once at fit time (`fit(OLSVAR, Y, p; dates=…)` / `VAR(Y, p; dates=…)`), stored
  lag-trimmed so they align with residual rows, and read automatically by the
  narrative `irf`/`rotation_matrix` path. When a model carries no dates,
  narrative restrictions fall back to integer residual-row indices; a
  date-based restriction on a date-less model still fails fast. This keeps a
  single specification path and removes the integer-vs-date asymmetry at the
  call site.

### CHUNK-002: finish-narrative-irf-path
- **Kind**: `investigate`
- **Description**: `NarrativeRestriction` is exported and constructible but `irf(model, ::NarrativeRestriction)` falls through to the generic `AbstractIdentification` method (`src/var/irfs.jl:226`) and errors at `rotation_matrix(model, identification)` (line 252) — no method exists. Audit what a narrative-identification IRF needs (it combines sign restrictions on the impact matrix with historical narrative sign constraints on structural shocks; the matrix-level checker `check_narrative_restrictions` already exists in `src/var/structural_core.jl`). Determine the `irf`/`rotation_matrix` shape required (likely a set-identified search like `SignRestriction`, returning `SignRestrictedIRFResult`), and whether a spoke already implements this. Output: a concrete implementation plan for CHUNK-003.
- **Status**: `complete`
- **Cluster**: narrative-restriction
- **Notes**: Investigation done 2026-06-30. Confirmed the failure: `NarrativeRestriction <: AbstractIdentification`, so `irf(model, ::NarrativeRestriction)` hits the generic single-`P` method at `src/var/irfs.jl:226`, which calls `rotation_matrix(model, identification)` (line 252) — and the only `rotation_matrix` methods are `CholeskyID`, `SignRestriction`, `IVIdentification` (`src/var/identification.jl`). No `NarrativeRestriction` method ⇒ `MethodError`. Even if one existed, narrative ID is set-identified, so the single-`P` `IRFResult` path is the wrong shape; it must mirror the `SignRestriction` multi-draw path returning `SignRestrictedIRFResult` (`src/var/irfs.jl:348–431`).

  **All matrix-level building blocks already exist** in `src/var/structural_core.jl`: `generate_random_orthogonal!`, `check_sign_restrictions(P, restrictions, Φ, horizon)` (the Φ-precomputed form, line 158), `compute_structural_shocks(U, P)` (line 197), `check_narrative_restrictions(ε, narrative_shocks, dates)` (line 208), `_resolve_narrative_date`. `NarrativeRestriction` carries `sign_restrictions::Matrix{Int}`, `narrative_shocks`, and `horizon` (`src/types.jl:832`).

  **Reference implementation exists in the spoke.** `BayesianVAR.jl/src/irf.jl:119–147` defines `rotation_matrix(Σ_L, B, U, id::NarrativeRestriction, n_vars, n_lags, rng; dates, max_attempts)` doing exactly the rejection search: draw `Q`, form `P = Σ_L*Q`, reject on `check_sign_restrictions`, then accept iff `check_narrative_restrictions(compute_structural_shocks(U, P), …)`. The hub method should follow this loop. Per the hub-spoke caution, the new hub `rotation_matrix(model::VARModel, ::NarrativeRestriction; …)` adds a *method* (new signature) and does not rename or change the spoke's matrix-level overload, so it is non-breaking for `BayesianVAR.jl` (its overload has a different, lower-level signature and stays intact).

  **Residuals/dates on the hub model.** `residuals(model)` returns `model.residuals` (n_obs_eff × n_vars), exactly the `U` needed. **The hub `VARModel` has no `dates` field** and its `metadata` (`src/var/estimation.jl:94`) carries no dates. Consequences for CHUNK-003: (a) integer-indexed `NarrativeShockRestriction`s work directly against the residual rows; (b) date-based restrictions cannot be auto-resolved — `_resolve_narrative_date` will `error(...)` when `dates===nothing`. The clean design is a `dates=nothing` kwarg on the new `irf`/`rotation_matrix` method so a caller can pass an aligned date vector (length = n_obs_eff, i.e. already lag-trimmed, matching how `BayesianVAR.jl` shifts dates by `n_lags`). Integer restrictions need no kwarg. Document that residual row `i` corresponds to date index `i`.

  **No `cumulate=` shortcut needed for v1**, but the `SignRestriction` path supports it; mirror it for parity (cheap, reuses `_cumulate_point!`).

### CHUNK-003: implement-narrative-irf
- **Kind**: `implement`
- **Description**: Implement the `irf` / `rotation_matrix` path for `NarrativeRestriction` per CHUNK-002's plan, so a constructed `NarrativeRestriction` produces an IRF result instead of a `MethodError`. Concrete shape (all helpers already in `src/var/structural_core.jl`; reference impl in `BayesianVAR.jl/src/irf.jl:119`):
  1. Add `rotation_matrix(model::VARModel{T}, id::NarrativeRestriction; max_draws=10000, dates=nothing, rng=...)` in `src/var/identification.jl`: get `Σ_L = cholesky(vcov(model)).L`, `U = residuals(model)`, `Φ = compute_ma_matrices(model.companion, id.horizon, n_vars, n_lags)`; loop up to `max_draws` drawing `Q` via `generate_random_orthogonal`, form `P = Σ_L*Q`, reject on `check_sign_restrictions(P, id.sign_restrictions, Φ, id.horizon)`, accept iff `check_narrative_restrictions(compute_structural_shocks(U, P), id.narrative_shocks, dates)`; `throw(ErrorException(...))` on exhaustion (fail-fast, mirror the `SignRestriction` message).
  2. Add `irf(model::VARModel{T}, id::NarrativeRestriction; n_draws=1000, max_attempts=10000, horizon=24, coverage, normalization, cumulate, scale, dates=nothing, rng)` in `src/var/irfs.jl` modeled on the `SignRestriction` method (`:348–431`): collect `n_draws` rotation matrices, build `irf_draws_raw`, quantile bands, median, and return `SignRestrictedIRFResult` (it already accepts `identification::SignRestriction` — widen that field's type, or store the narrative id; check `src/types.jl:656`). **Decide during impl**: either loosen `SignRestrictedIRFResult.identification` to `AbstractIdentification` (non-breaking widening) or introduce a parallel result type. Prefer widening.
  3. Thread `dates` through; integer restrictions need no dates. Document residual-row alignment.
  - Tests: a 2–3 var VAR with an integer-indexed `NarrativeShockRestriction` (+ optional sign matrix) returns a `SignRestrictedIRFResult` of the right dims; a date-based restriction without `dates=` errors clearly; result is reproducible under a seeded `rng`. Run the suite and `Test.detect_ambiguities` (baseline 0).
- **Status**: `complete`
- **Depends on**: CHUNK-002
- **Cluster**: narrative-restriction
- **Notes**: Implemented 2026-06-30. Added `rotation_matrix(model::VARModel,
  ::NarrativeRestriction; max_draws, rng)` (`src/var/identification.jl`) doing the
  rejection search via the existing `structural_core.jl` helpers, and
  `irf(model::VARModel, ::NarrativeRestriction; …)` (`src/var/irfs.jl`) mirroring
  the `SignRestriction` multi-draw path, returning `SignRestrictedIRFResult`.
  **Widened `SignRestrictedIRFResult.identification` to `::AbstractIdentification`**
  (`src/types.jl`) — audited first: no spoke references `SignRestrictedIRFResult`
  or dispatches on that field, so the widening is safe (non-breaking).
  `detect_ambiguities` stayed at 0.

  **Dates design changed from the original plan** per author decision (see

  Added a `dates` kwarg to `fit(OLSVAR, …)` (validated length == n_obs, stored

### CHUNK-008: fix-axes-import-cumulate
- **Kind**: `implement`
- **Description**: `_cumulate_point!` and the quantile helpers in `src/var/irfs.jl`
  (lines 131, 163, 688, 759) call bare `axes`, but `axes` is not imported into the
  module (`isdefined(MacroEconometricTools, :axes) == false`) — a fallout of the
  explicit-imports cleanup in `b6dc4b3`. Any `irf(model, ::SignRestriction;
  cumulate=…)` (and the new `::NarrativeRestriction` cumulate path) throws
  `UndefVarError: 'axes' not defined`. Fix by adding `axes` to the package's
  imports (e.g. a `Base: axes` import alongside the other explicit `using`s in
  `src/MacroEconometricTools.jl`), or qualify the call sites. Add a regression
  test exercising `irf(…; cumulate=[…])` for a sign restriction (no existing test
  covers this path, which is why the regression went undetected). Non-breaking.
- **Status**: `complete`
- **Notes**: 2026-06-30. **The import-fix premise was invalidated by direct
  verification.** Bare `axes` in `src/var/irfs.jl` (lines 131, 163, 687, 758)
  resolves to `Base.axes` on **both** supported Julia versions — running every
  public cumulate path (`irf(::SignRestriction; cumulate=Int|Symbol)`,
  `cumulative_irf(::SignRestrictedIRFResult)`, `irf(::CholeskyID; inference,
  cumulate)`, `cumulative_irf(::IRFResult)`) succeeds on Julia 1.10.11 (the
  compat floor) and 1.12.6. No `UndefVarError` occurs; `isdefined(M, :axes)` is
  `true` on both. The original `isdefined == false` reading was a transient
  Revise-session measurement artifact, never cross-checked by running the path.
  **No import was added** — a spurious `axes` import would be unjustified and
  flagged by ExplicitImports as stale.

  The genuinely missing half — **no test covered any `cumulate=` /
  `cumulative_irf` path** — was real and is now closed. Added a "Cumulative IRF
  paths" testset to `test/test_sign_restrictions.jl` (14 assertions) exercising
  all four call sites end-to-end and asserting the running-sum semantics. For
  the set-identified (sign-restriction) paths the invariant is checked
  **draw-by-draw** (each cumulated draw == `cumsum` of its un-cumulated draw),
  not on the recomputed median: cumulation happens per draw and the median is
  recomputed afterward, so `median∘cumsum ≠ cumsum∘median`. For the Cholesky
  point-estimate path the linear `cumsum` identity holds directly. Suite green
  (sign 20, narrative 133, cumulative 14); ambiguities 0. Tests-only change,
  non-breaking. Staged, not committed.
